blocks.h2: Water Filtration Options for Elgin Homes

tiles.body: Reduce chlorine and the taste and odor changes that come and go with river water.
Under-sink reverse osmosis or carbon for cooking and drinking.
Cut the minerals that leave spots, scale and sediment in the water heater.
Catch rust and particles, common in older homes with galvanized pipe.

bodies: Elgin is one of the few cities in the area that drinks treated Fox River water. The Riverside plant has treated it since 1982, and the Airlite plant adds well water. River water changes with the seasons: heavy rain and drought both affect what the plant has to treat, which is why taste can shift during the year.

A test at your tap shows hardness, chlorine, iron and other things that affect taste, scale and appliances. It also shows what your own pipes add. In older homes, that's often rust from galvanized pipe. We use the results to recommend only what your home needs.

blocks.intro: The city treats your water to drinking water standards. What you notice at the tap depends on the season and your pipes.

items.body: Because Elgin draws from the Fox River, taste and odor can change after storms or during dry summers. A carbon filter smooths those changes out at the tap.
Homes built before 1940 may still have galvanized supply lines. Rust-colored water and low pressure point to the pipe, not the city water. [Leak and pipe repair](/elgin/leak-repairs) fixes the cause.
If you see white crust on showerheads or spots on glasses, a softener or scale filter may help. A test tells you if it's worth it.

blocks.h2: Water Filtration Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Where does Elgin's water come from?
items.preview: Mostly the Fox River, treated at the Riverside plant, plus well water from the Airlite plant.
items.answer: Elgin treats Fox River water at its Riverside plant and adds well water from the Airlite plant. The city publishes a yearly water quality report with the details.

items.q: Why does my water taste different in summer?
items.preview: River water changes with weather. A carbon filter helps.
items.answer: River water quality changes with rain, heat and drought, and treatment changes with it. Most of what you taste is safe but noticeable. A carbon filter evens it out.

items.q: Do I need a water softener in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on your water and preferences. Test first.
items.answer: It depends on your water and how much scale bothers you. A test shows hardness at your tap so you can decide with real numbers.

items.q: How often do I change the filters?
items.preview: Most cartridges every few months to a year.
items.answer: It depends on the system and your water use. Most cartridges last a few months to a year. We'll set you up with a schedule.

items.q: How much does a water filtration system cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on the system. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the type of system, its size and how it connects to your plumbing. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
